questions.title: α + β + αβ for x² − ax − b
questions.text: If α and β are the zeroes of the polynomial p(x) = x² − ax − b, then the value of (α + β + αβ) is equal to:
steps: ① Sum of zeroes: α + β = −(coefficient of x) / (coefficient of x²)
∴ α + β + αβ = a + (−b) = a − b → (c)
questions.trap: Mixing up the letter 'a' in the question with the coefficient a. Write the coefficients first.
questions.tryit: α, β are zeroes of x² − 5x + 6. Find α + β − αβ.

questions.title: Zeroes of x² − 3√2x + 4
questions.text: Zeroes of the polynomial p(x) = x² − 3√2x + 4 are:
steps: ① Shortcut: test the options with sum and product
② Sum must be 3√2,  product must be 4
questions.remember: In an MCQ, test each option with sum and product. Faster than solving!
questions.trap: Option (a) has sum 2 + √2, not 3√2. Always check BOTH conditions.

questions.title: α + β = αβ for px² − 2x + 3p: find p
questions.text: If α and β are the zeroes of a polynomial f(x) = px² − 2x + 3p and α + β = αβ, then the value of p is:
steps: ① Coefficients: a = p,  b = −2,  c = 3p
questions.remember: A condition on the zeroes? Turn it into an equation using sum and product.
questions.trap: Writing the sum as −2/p. Minus of minus 2 is PLUS 2.
questions.tryit: The product of the zeroes of kx² + 4x + 5 is 3. Find k.

questions.title: Assertion–Reason: reciprocal zeroes
questions.text:
Assertion (A): If the zeroes of the polynomial (2k − 1)x² + 4x − 3 are reciprocal of each other, then k = −1.
Reason (R): If a = c, then the zeroes of the polynomial ax² + bx + c, a ≠ 0, are reciprocal of each other.
opts: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
steps: ① Reciprocal zeroes: α and 1/α ⟹ product = α × 1/α = 1
② Product = c/a = 1 ⟹ a = c  ✓ R true
⑤ A used exactly the condition in R
questions.trap: Finding k, then not checking whether R was actually used. Here, it was!
questions.tryit: For what k are the zeroes of kx² + 3x + 5 reciprocal?

questions.title: α⁴β³ + α³β⁴ for y² − 5y + 3
questions.text: If α and β are the zeroes of the polynomial p(y) = y² − 5y + 3, then find the value of α⁴β³ + α³β⁴.
steps: ② Common part: α⁴β³ + α³β⁴ = α³β³(α + β)
questions.remember: Take out the common factor, then use only α + β and αβ.
questions.trap: Finding α and β separately. They're irrational here and it wastes time.

questions.title: α³β + β³α for px² + qx + r
questions.text: If α, β are the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial px² + qx + r, then find the value of α³β + β³α.
questions.trap: Writing α² + β² = (α + β)². Don't forget the −2αβ!
questions.tryit: α, β are zeroes of x² − 7x + 10. Find α² + β².

questions.title: Zeroes of 3x² − 4x − 4, then shift each by 2
questions.text: Find the zeroes of the polynomial p(x) = 3x² − 4x − 4. Hence, write a polynomial whose each of the zeroes is 2 more than zeroes of p(x).
questions.trap: Adding 2 to the coefficients instead of to the zeroes.
questions.tryit: Find a quadratic polynomial whose zeroes are 3 and −5.

questions.title: Case study: the arch p(x) = −x² + 2x + 8
questions.text:
In a theatre drama, the backdrop shows arches of a building. The curve of an arch is p(x) = −x² + 2x + 8, where x is the length (in feet) along the stage.
(i) Find the height of the arch.  (ii) Find the zeroes of p(x) and the span of the arch.  (iii) Where does the curve meet the y-axis?
questions.remember: Zeroes = where the graph meets the x-axis. The top of a symmetric arch is midway between them.
questions.trap: Taking the y-intercept (8) as the height. The top is at x = 1, not x = 0.

questions.tryit: For the same arch, find p(3).
